note: Rob's live collection, built by tools/build-live-load.mjs from the Master workbook; CrankMagic → User Functions → Load Live reads this file. Card names are exact Scryfall names (double-faced cards use 'Front // Back'). decks[].cards is the 100-card target; owned.inDeck is what is physically in each deck box; owned.bench is everything else owned; ordered is in flight; buy is the outstanding shopping list; upgrades are optional ceiling cards with the slot each replaces; decks[].options are cards in the hundred flagged as the first to swap out; decks[].planned are cards meant to come into the deck that are not in its hundred yet. Rebuild from the workbook rather than editing quantities here; names, definitions, notes, options and planned lists are carried over per deck.

decks.name: D1 Quintorius Spirits
decks.notes: Cards LEAVING your graveyard make 3/2 Spirits. Fill the bin, exile from it repeatedly, sac Spirits to free-cast what you exiled. Midrange grind. Win through recursion value and a wide Spirit alpha, not speed.
cards: Fable of the Mirror-Breaker // Reflection of Kiki-Jiki
Kirol, History Buff // Pack a Punch

decks.name: D2 Chulane Value Loop
decks.notes: Every creature CAST draws a card and gives a land drop. Blink/bounce cheap ETB bodies to loop value. Combo-value. Ramp hard, land Chulane, chain creatures, finish wide or on a loop.
cards: Bilbo Baggins, Burglar // Take a Glance

decks.name: D3 Atraxa Proliferate
decks.notes: Free end-step proliferate compounds every counter. Win on poison, +1/+1 counters, or charge-counter engines. Four-colour grind. Survive, spread counters, let proliferate double them.
cards: The Restoration of Eiganjo // Architect of Restoration

decks.name: D4 Felothar Walls
decks.notes: High-toughness walls that deal damage equal to toughness and can attack. Block all game, then alpha. Defensive fortress. Take no damage, one-sided wipe, swing once for lethal.

options.why: Four basics come out for the two dorks and two rocks coming in (any four)

decks.name: D5 Shadrix Aristocrats
decks.notes: Flood the board with tokens; each body drains on entry and again on death. Wide aristocrats grind. Bodies + drain payoffs + a sac outlet.

decks.name: D6 Krenko Goblins
decks.notes: Krenko doubles the goblin count each tap; ETB-damage engines turn tokens into reach. Fast mono-red swarm. Fastest clock of the six; win before the table stabilises.

upgrades.why: Mana equal to an opponent's hand plus three cards off the top. It is the turn where Quintorius goes from grinding to winning.
Every spell you cast from the graveyard is a card leaving the graveyard, so every one is also a Spirit. This is the deck's engine, not a value piece.
Exiles a spell out of the graveyard and copies it. Two Quintorius triggers and a free sorcery in one card.
Scales every combat instead of a five-mana spell that does not touch the graveyard.
Four damage, or team indestructible through a wipe, or double strike. Three answers on one card instead of one.
A free sacrifice outlet turns every Spirit into damage. The deck makes bodies and currently has no way to cash them in.
Repeatable creature recursion every turn, and the token is exiled at end of turn so the card leaves the graveyard again.
Tutors any instant in the deck straight onto the stack. Consistency for a deck built on the right answer at the right time.
Two permanents back at instant speed for two mana, and two cards leaving the graveyard means two Spirits.
One mana of insurance against the wipe that otherwise ends your game.
Tutors any creature to the battlefield, and for large X it is the game-ending pump. One card that is both the setup and the finish.
Doubles every enter-the-battlefield trigger you have and shuts off every one your opponents have. In a deck built on ETBs this is two cards in one.
With Chulane out, two cheap creatures bounce each other forever. This is the card that turns the deck from good value into a combo deck.
Blinks a nonland permanent every time you cast a noncreature spell. Free value on cards you were casting anyway.
The best card selection in green. Fixes the draws where Chulane never lands.
Same-turn kill off either infinite loop. Cut on second review; Approach does it for a third of the price.
Hexproof and indestructible at instant speed. Cut on second review in favour of Unbreakable Formation at $0.74.
A card every time a nontoken creature enters. Chulane already draws you one; this doubles it.
A blink outlet that costs three and needs no blue, and it grows the creature it blinks.
A card on every creature spell instead of a card once.
Two blinks for one card, and it can reset lands as well as creatures.
Overloaded it bounces every nonland permanent your opponents control at instant speed. It is the single best turn this deck can have.
Doubles every counter you place and halves every counter your opponents get. Atraxa's proliferate becomes twice as fast and their proliferate stops working.
The wipe answer the deck does not have. Phases out everything you own and makes you untargetable until your next turn.
A one-sided wipe. Everything without a +1/+1 counter dies, and your board is made of +1/+1 counters.
Two mana to save the entire board. The second layer of wipe insurance behind Teferi's Protection.
One-sided -1/-1 wipe plus a second proliferate every turn. Cut on second review; Fall of the First Civilization does the wipe job free.
A +1/+1 counter on every creature you control every time a creature enters. It compounds with every token and every proliferate.
Every creature with a counter becomes unblockable. It turns a stalled counters board into lethal.
Doubles the counters on every creature you control whenever it attacks.
A card on every creature spell in the deck with the most creatures.
One mana, and it gives a creature protection to dodge removal or to push damage through.
Doubles every counter that would be placed on your creatures for four mana.
Every creature you cast arrives with counters already on it. The Hexmage removes counters, which fights your own plan.
Two mana to protect the board you spent the game assembling.
All damage to your creatures becomes +1/+1 counters instead. In a toughness deck it makes combat unlosable.
Opponents cannot cast spells or activate abilities during your turn. Your wipe and your alpha both resolve untouched.
A fifth global toughness-as-damage body. Cut from the order on second review; the deck has four already.
Life equal to toughness every time a creature enters, and your creatures are all toughness.
Taxes every attack against you. A defensive deck should be nearly unattackable.
Toughness with no ceiling, and Betor counts total toughness.
Indestructible and flying on top of the pump, so the creature survives wipes and gets through.
A creature back from the graveyard every turn, for thirty-three cents.
Plus zero plus two to the whole team pushes several creatures over Betor's next threshold at once.
Ramp and fixing in the three-color deck with the fewest mana sources to spare.
Life every time a defender blocks, which is every combat in this deck. (v12: Jaddi Offshoot left the deck; the Ram is the other lifegain wall.)
A 0/6 that returns to your hand every time it blocks. Thirty cents for an infinite blocker.
Every creature that dies on your side makes each opponent sacrifice one. With tokens dying constantly it dismantles three boards at once.
The same effect as Grave Pact with flash, so it lands after a wipe and punishes it.
Play off the top of your library paying life instead of mana. In a deck already gaining life it is close to a free win.
Every token you would make becomes a 4/4 Angel instead. Forty-four cents, and it is the biggest single upgrade on this entire tab.
Fifth free outlet and two mana per body. Cut from the order on second review because four free outlets already exist; still the best single upgrade for the deck.
A +1/+1 counter on everything each time a creature enters. Your tokens stop being 1/1s.
A treasure, a body and a card every turn, all optional, all at the cost of some life you are already gaining back.
Prevents the attack that would kill you and turns the damage into that many 1/1 fliers.
Grows on every death and then dies into an army of Vampires.
Counters on your creatures and a 2/1 Inkling every time one with a counter dies.
Counters and cards every time an opponent is attacked, including by someone who is not you.
Any card in the deck for four mana. Slow, but it finds Grave Pact or the Altar when the game demands it.
A card each turn you made a token, which is nearly every turn.
Every goblin gets plus one plus one for every other goblin. Thirty tokens becomes lethal instead of chip damage.
Copy Krenko every turn. Each copy taps for goblins equal to your goblin count, and the count doubles as it goes.
Look at the top six and put every goblin onto the battlefield. It refills a wiped board in one card.
Three mana untaps Krenko. With enough goblins producing mana, that is arbitrarily many goblins in one turn.
One damage on turn two puts Krenko or Muxus onto the battlefield for free.
Stacks the top of your library with exactly the goblins you need, in the order you need them.
Goblins you cast get menace and dead goblins come back off the top. Recursion in the color that has almost none.
